correctness.rationale: For the continuous-time SIR process with one infectious seed and homogeneous edge rate beta, event-clock conditioning gives an acyclic recursion for expected absorption time h and expected subsequent infections f. Independently recomputed every graph–missing-edge–seed triple on n<=3: exactly 38 labeled cases, with symbolic nonnegative differences for all beta>0, including disconnected graphs. For a four-cycle with edges 02,03,12,13 and seed 2, inserting diagonal 01 at beta=10 changes mean duration by -1631125/648015984 and expected final infections by +8200/586971; exact-rational independent computation matched both. This is a witness at n=4, not an exhaustive four-vertex classification. It uses mathematical coefficient positivity, not finite beta sampling, for the all-rate lower bound.

value.rationale: A sharp counterexample to intuitive contact-addition duration monotonicity is meaningful: greater final epidemic size need not mean longer epidemic duration. Four vertices is a natural minimal boundary and the exact witness is relevant to stochastic network-process comparisons, independent of general CTMC computability.

limitations: Unconditional continuous-time duration from one fixed seed; no graph-size extension.
Only homogeneous exponential infection/recovery rates, no reinfection or interventions.
